## Day 3 — Everyone in the shop has read the booking password taped under the register, so it must be fine.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0016`  
**Image:** `gm-social-digital-solutions-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Sat Nov 21, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
Everyone in the shop has read the booking password taped under the register, so it must be fine.
That is the belief. Here is what is true. A shared password cannot be changed without breaking every device that uses it, and you cannot tell who used it on a bad day.
Trusted people still leave. Phones get lost. Passwords end up on sticky notes and in group texts.
Give each person their own login. Turn on two-step sign-in for the booking system and the shop email. When someone leaves, you turn off one account instead of changing everything.

See how it works: https://graymatterdigitalsolutions.com/services/business-security.html

#GrayMatter #MontgomeryAL #SmallBusiness #SmallBusinessSecurity
```

## Day 4 — Sunday night, a customer emails asking for a quote, and the price sheet is on the shop computer.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0025`  
**Image:** `gm-social-digital-solutions-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Sun Nov 22, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
Sunday night, a customer emails asking for a quote, and the price sheet is on the shop computer.

The shop computer is locked in a building you left at six. So the reply waits until Monday, and by Monday the customer has booked someone who answered faster.

This is the one-desk problem. The business only moves when you sit in front of one machine. The fix is not a faster computer. It is making your files and email reachable from a phone or laptop, with logins only you and trusted people can use.

Start small. Write down the three documents you reach for most, and make sure they can be opened from anywhere.

See how it works: https://graymatterdigitalsolutions.com/services/work-from-anywhere.html
```

## Day 7 — Myth: the AI tool you used at lunch is private because its homepage says so.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0036`  
**Image:** `gm-social-technology-partner-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Wed Nov 25, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
Myth: the AI tool you used at lunch is private because its homepage says so.

What's true is that you have to read what it does with what you type. Does it keep your messages? Does it use them to train its models? Does it share them with other companies?

Look for those answers in the privacy terms, not on the homepage. If a company plans to start using your data in a new way, it should tell you clearly and ask first.

Until you know, keep client phone numbers, card details and appointment history out of the box. Use it for drafting the sign on the wall or a thank-you text, not the client file.

Which task would you hand to an AI tool first?

Tell us what needs to change. We figure out the technology: https://graymatterdigitalsolutions.com/contact.html

#GrayMatter #MontgomeryAL #SmallBusiness
```

## Day 8 — The invoice looked exactly like the last one from the lumber supplier.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0019`  
**Image:** `gm-social-digital-solutions-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Thu Nov 26, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
The invoice looked exactly like the last one from the lumber supplier.
Same logo, same amount, same signature. The only change was a new bank account at the bottom.
The office manager paid it that afternoon. Later that week the supplier called, asking where the money was.
This kind of fake invoice scam works because the email looks normal. Before you pay any changed bank details, call the supplier on a number you already had, not the one in the email. Ask them to confirm the new account.

Has a supplier ever asked you to send money to a new bank account?

Tell us what needs to change. We figure out the technology: https://graymatterdigitalsolutions.com/contact.html
```

## Day 9 — Myth: you need a full binder before Saturday closing steps are worth writing down.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0028`  
**Image:** `gm-social-digital-solutions-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Fri Nov 27, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
Myth: you need a full binder before Saturday closing steps are worth writing down.

What's true is smaller. Start with the one job that goes wrong when you're not in the chair. Maybe it's the color mix, the booking rules for new clients, or how you close the shop on Saturdays.

Write those steps down in plain words, the way you would explain them to a new hire standing next to you. Five short steps beat a binder nobody opens.

Then test the written procedure. Hand the steps to someone on your team and watch where they get stuck. Fix the gap, and keep the page where people can find it.

Build your plan in a couple of minutes, no call required: https://graymatterdigitalsolutions.com/#build-my-plan

#GrayMatter #MontgomeryAL #SmallBusiness
```

## Day 12 — Sunday night, you retype a full-detail deposit from a DM you saved.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0042`  
**Image:** `gm-social-workflow-automation-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Mon Nov 30, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
Sunday night, you retype a full-detail deposit from a DM you saved.

Four things to check before the next one.

Find the last three DMs that said "book me in." Count how many times you copied the same name, car and address.

Look at where the deposit is recorded. If it lives in a text thread, a notebook and a bank app, pick one place.

Compare the phone number in each app. If they do not match, choose the correct one and fix the rest the same day.

Check whether the confirmed time is on the calendar you open on Sunday night, not just the one in your truck.

Any step you repeat every week is the first one worth handing off.
```

## Day 13 — The laptop slid off the passenger seat on the way to a job and hit the curb.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0022`  
**Image:** `gm-social-digital-solutions-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Tue Dec 01, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
The laptop slid off the passenger seat on the way to a job and hit the curb.
The screen cracked and the drive would not start. Every customer address, every photo of finished work and every scanned contract was on it.
Nothing had been copied anywhere else. That evening the owner of the small business rebuilt the client list from texts and memory.
A backup is a second copy stored somewhere else, and it only counts after you have restored something from it. Check when your last backup finished, then ask yourself when you last opened a file from it.

When did you last copy your job files anywhere besides the laptop?
```

## Day 14 — Before you ask three shops for a quote on new computers, gather these four things.

**Post ID:** `gm-fb-0032`  
**Image:** `gm-social-technology-checkup-square.png`  
**Suggested date:** Wed Dec 02, 2026  
**Approval:** approved

### Facebook text

```
Before you ask three shops for a quote on new computers, gather these four things.

List the devices your crew uses, including phones and the old laptop in the back office.

List the accounts: email, bank, card processor, website, and who owns each login.

Note what happens today when something breaks. Who do you call, and how long can the business run without it?

Note every monthly charge, even the small ones.

Then ask for quotes. You'll get answers you can compare against your own list instead of guesses. If you can't fill in the list, that's a sign the first step is a review, not a purchase.

Which of these four things would you have to start from scratch today?

Not sure where to start? Start with a Business Technology Checkup: https://graymatterdigitalsolutions.com/services/business-technology-checkup.html
```
